name: Ubayd ibn al-Abras
bio: Ubayd ibn al-Abras, also written Abid, was a pre-Islamic poet of Asad known as Abu Ziyad. Tradition credits him with exchanges in verse with his contemporary Imru' al-Qays. Abu Zayd al-Qurashi included his ode on the deserted site of Malhub among the Mujamharat, and al-Tibrizi commented on it among the ten odes. An account from Hisham ibn al-Kalbi says that al-Mundhir ibn Ma' al-Sama', king of al-Hira, killed him when he arrived on the king's appointed day of ill fortune. Al-Zirikli names the king as al-Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir and tentatively dates the poet's death to about 600 CE.
